'''Takihara Shrine''' (多岐原神社, *Takihara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}} (the Inner Shrine) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}. It was established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, who enshrined the local {{ill|Deity|af|Godheid|anp|देवता|ar|إله|ary|رب|az|İlah|bat_smg|Dievībė|be|Бажаство|bg|Божество|bn|দেবতা|br|Doueelezh|ca|Deïtat|ckb|خوداوەندی|cy|Duwdod|da|Gud (højere væsen)|dag|Baɣyuli Pulibu|el|Θεότητα|eo|Diaĵo|es|Deidad|et|Jumalus|eu|Jainko (politeismo)|fa|الوهیت|fi|Jumalolento|fiu_vro|Jumalus|fr|Divinité|fy|God|gcr|Divinité|gl|Deidade|guc|Ma'leiwa|he|אל|hif|Deity|hr|Božanstvo|ht|Divinite|hu|Istenség|hy|Աստվածություն|ia|Deitate|id|Dewa|io|Deajo|is|Goð|ja|神|jam|Diiyti|jbo|cevni|jv|Déwa|kbp|Ɛsɔ kɛtʊ|kk|Құдірет|kn|ದೇವರು|ko|신|ku|Xwedawend|kw|Duwses|la|Divinitas|lfn|Divin|lld|Divinité|lmo|Dia|lo|ເທວະດາ|lt|Dievybė|lv|Dievība|mg|Andriamanitra (ankapobeny)|min|Dewa|mk|Божество|mn|Дейти|ms|Dewa|my|ကြီးမြတ်မှုအရာ|nah|Teōtl|nl|God (algemeen)|no|Guddom|oc|Deitat|pa|ਦੇਵਤਾ|pap|Dios|pt|Deidade|qu|Thiyus kay|ro|Zeitate|ru|Божество|sd|ديوي ديوتا|sh|Božanstvo|si|දෙවි දේවතාවියෝ|simple|Deity|sl|Božanstvo|sn|Munamatwi|sq|Hyjnitë|sr|Божанство|st|Molimo|sv|Gudom|sw|Miungu|szy|di'tu, dietu|th|เทวภาพ|tl|Pagkadiyos|tok|jan sewi|tr|İlahi varlık|tum|Chata|ug|ئىلاھ|uk|Боги|ur|معبود|vi|Thần|wuu|神|zh|神|zh_min_nan|Sîn-bêng|zh_yue|神祇|qid=Q178885|lt=kami}} in gratitude for its assistance<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 84</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 73</ref>.

The shrine is located along the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie)}} with the gentle murmur of the river resonating through the trees of the precincts<ref name="ic"/>.

== Overview ==

{{ill|Takihara Shrine|ja|多岐原神社}} is located in {{ill|Misedagawa|ja|三瀬川}}, {{ill|Taiki, Mie|arz|تايكى|ceb|Taiki Chō (subdistrito sa Hapon, Mie-ken)|ckb|تایکی (میێ)|es|Taiki (Mie)|fa|تائیکی، میئه|fr|Taiki (Mie)|hy|Տայկի|id|Taiki, Mie|it|Taiki|ja|大紀町|ko|다이키정 (미에현)|ms|Taiki, Mie|my|တိုင်းခိမြို့၊ မိအဲ|pl|Taiki|ru|Тайки (Миэ)|sv|Taiki, Mie|tl|Taiki, Mie|tr|Taiki, Mie|uk|Тайкі (Міє)|vi|Taiki, Mie|zh|大紀町|qid=Q1203189|lt=Ōdai, Mie}}, [[:en:Watarai District, Mie|Watarai District, Mie]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 227</ref>. It lies approximately 6 km downstream along the {{ill|Miyagawa|de|Miyagawa|fr|Miyagawa|ja|宮川|ko|미야가와|ru|Миягава|qid=Q1665818|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie)}} from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮}}<ref name="ic"/>. Among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Naikū|ja|内宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naikū (Ise Grand Shrine)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q23996212}}, it Ranks 27th<ref>Ujiyamada City Office (1929): pp. 9-11</ref>. Unlike most auxiliary shrines of Ise Jingū, which typically do not have offering boxes<ref>Ise Bunkasha (2008): p. 26</ref>, Takihara Shrine does have one.

The shrine building is constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|es|Shinmeizukuri|fr|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|ru|Симмэй-дзукури|tr|Shinmei-zukuri|zh|神明造|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} architectural style with a wooden plank roof, facing south<ref name="sk8">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 228</ref>. The shrine precinct is enclosed by a single layer of {{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=Tamagaki}} fencing, and features a {{ill|Torii|ja|神明鳥居|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei torii|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鳥居|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q234731}}<ref name="sk8"/>. The shrine grounds cover an area of approximately 5,890.9 square meters<ref name="uy">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p. 11</ref>.

== Enshrined deity ==

The enshrined deity is {{ill|Manago no Kami|ja|真奈胡神}} (pronounced "manago no kami"<ref name="ic"/> or "manako no kami"<ref name="gk"/>). According to legend, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was struggling to cross a rapid current when Manago no Kami assisted her<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>. Although scholar Nakagawa Tsunemasa interpreted the name "Manako" as "眞之子" ("true child"), implying that this deity might be the offspring of the deity enshrined at Takihara-no-Miya, the true origin remains unclear<ref name="sk7"/>.

== Shrine Name ==

In historical records, the shrine is referred to with various kanji, including "瀧原" in the {{ill|Enryaku Gishikichō|ja|皇太神宮儀式帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū Gishikichō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延暦儀式帳|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q109596938}} and "多伎原" or "多紀原" in different manuscripts of the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. The current standard form "多岐原" was adopted in later periods<ref name="sk7"/>. In the {{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記}}, it is listed as "御瀬社"<ref name="sk7"/>.

Locally, it is affectionately called "{{ill|Manago-san|ja|まなごさん}}"<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>, and serves as a substitute for ancestral shrine rituals following the relocation of the original {{ill|Ujigami|en|Ujigami|qid=Q767655|lt=Ujigami}}<ref name="st">Sakurai (1991): pp. 293-294</ref>.

== History ==

According to legends recorded in texts such as the Yamato-hime-no-mikoto-seiki, Yamato-hime-no-mikoto, while carrying the sacred spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, attempted to cross the fast-flowing Miyagawa River. Manago no Kami guided her across, and the shrine was established in commemoration of this event<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 227-228</ref>. Historically, the shrine was founded before the compilation of the Engishiki Jinmyōchō in 927 AD<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunkasha (2008): p. 22</ref>. It is also mentioned in the Kōtai Jingū Gishikichō, indicating its existence before 804 AD<ref name="sk7"/><ref name="ic2"/>.

In 1663, the shrine was restored by Ōmiya-shi {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} (Ōnakatomi Masanaga)<ref name="sk7"/>. Though it is unclear whether the current site is the original location, geographical features and legends suggest continuity<ref name="sk7"/>. In 1724, the {{ill|Kishū Domain|de|Kishū (Han)|es|Dominio de Kishū|fa|قلمرو کیشو|fr|Domaine de Kishū|ja|紀州藩|ko|기슈번|pt|Domínio de Wakayama|ru|Кисю (княжество)|zh|紀州藩|qid=Q1069187|lt=Kishu Domain}} erected a "prohibition of killing" stone marker, and in 1732, two {{ill|Nightlight|ar|مصباح ليلي|az|Gecə lampası|ca|Llum de vetlla|de|Nachtorientierungslicht|fa|چراغ خواب|fr|Veilleuse|he|מנורת לילה|hy|Գիշերալամպ|ja|常夜灯|ko|종야등|nds_nl|Nachlampjen|nl|Nachtlamp (lamp)|no|Nattarmatur|ru|Ночник|sv|Nattlampa|tr|Gece lambası|uk|Нічник|zh|夜燈|qid=Q762277|lt=Chōchin}} lanterns were donated by the village of Misekawa<ref name="sk8"/>.

The shrine building was reconstructed in October 1904<ref name="uy"/>.

== Mitsesaka Pass and Mitsese Crossing Site ==

The route connecting Takihara Shrine and Takihara-no-Miya is part of the {{ill|Iseji Route|ja|伊勢路|qid=Q11379139}} of the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|qid=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodo}}, a pilgrimage path leading to the {{ill|Kumano shrine|ja|熊野三山|pl|Kumano Sanzan|ru|Три храма Кумано|zh|熊野三山|qid=Q10403700|lt=Kumano Sanzan}}<ref>Ise Bunkasha (2008): pp. 84, 86</ref><ref name="gk"/>. The path includes the Mitsesaka Pass, characterized by steep inclines<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic"/>. Though not part of the UNESCO World Heritage "Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range," remnants such as old teahouse sites and the Hōreki Jizō statue remain<ref>Ise Bunkasha (2008): p. 86</ref>.

About 150 meters from Takihara Shrine lies the site of the "Mitsese Crossing," once part of the Iseji Route<ref name="gk"/>. Post-war river improvements have altered the landscape<ref name="sk7"/>.

== Rituals ==

The shrine hosts the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai}} on February 19, {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}} on June 22 and December 22, and the {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}} on October 22<ref name="sk8"/>.

After the local ujigami was merged with another shrine 4.36 km away in 1908, the community began holding their {{ill|Kōshin-machi|ja|庚申待}} ritual at Takihara Shrine on June 19, and a rice-cake throwing event on February 9 as a substitute for the former "Mikuwajinji" ritual<ref name="st"/>.

== Access ==

; Public Transport
Takihara Shrine is approximately 3.6 km from {{ill|Misedani Station|en|Misedani Station|qid=Q5357769|lt=Misedani Station}} on the JR {{ill|Kisei Main Line|en|Kisei Main Line|qid=Q582803|lt=Kisei Main Line}}, about a 1 hour and 8-minute walk<ref name="ic2"/>. Signboards are posted nearby<ref name="ic"/>.

; By Car
About 4 minutes (3.4 km) via {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 747|ja|三重県道747号打見大台線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 747|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11358134}} from {{ill|Omiya-Odai interchange|ja|大宮大台インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-Ōdai IC|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10934923}} on the {{ill|Kisei Expressway|en|Kisei Expressway|qid=Q6416449|lt=Kisei Expressway}}.
